text.p: Bonds closed sharply higher but did not keep pace with the buoyant Bonos and Italian market.
The spread with the 10-year cash Spanish equivalent narrowed to one basis point from eight on Monday. The local market was closed on Tuesday for the National Day holiday.

Traders said that there was growing optimism European Union countries would patch up their differences over the stability pact after France's Socialist-led government expressed concern at the lack of any commitment to promoting employment in Europe.
The dispute had led to doubts about whether the single currency would be launched on time in January 1999.
"The market believes that Germany and France...are going to reach agreement on the inclusion of clauses over growth and employment," said one fixed income trader.
"Despite lacking the strength of the Bonos, the 10-year consolidated a spread under 75 basis points (vs Bund). This level is perfectly sustainable," the trader added.
Another trader said that the market had ended the session well "bid" and should widen the spread with Bonos on Thursday ahead of Friday's Lisbon market close.
But several traders saw more upside in the short end which had failed to accompany the gains at the longer end on Wednesday, leading to a flattening of the curve.
"It is illogical...because we know that if there is a single currency in 1999, the money should be invested at the short end," added another trader.

The March 99 closed with a yield of 5.34 percent, 22 basis points above the Bono equivalent. The spread between the Portuguese two and 10 year cash bonds narrowed to 116 basis points from 121 on Monday.
